faq.a: Ebrahim is associated with the Hebrew form إبراهيم, whose core sense is father of many, father of multitudes.

faq.q: What is the origin of Ebrahim?
faq.a: Ebrahim is associated with Hebrew. Variant romanization of إبراهيم (Abraham), a prophet named in the Qur'an. The source record's gloss 'Father of Many' is a reasonable rendering.
No — the underlying form is Hebrew, not Arabic.
Ebrahim can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Hebrew-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Ebrahim should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. إبراهيم is named in the Qur'an (e.g. 2:124)

faq.a: Romanization variants include Ebrahim, ebrahim. Script forms are إبراهيم, ابراهیم, ابراہیم, इब्राहीम.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
